details: Principle 6: evidence first, then one fix for the runner deaths.
failing_case: An agent that throws once and succeeds on retry leaves no trace of the error.
pass_cases: Each thrown attempt writes its message, label and time to $S/reports/dead-<label>-<n>.txt before the retry.
An agent that does not throw leaves no file.
findings.summary: A dead workflow agent leaves no error text

details: CONFIRMED by reading and by a probe. lib/relay_labels.py: a label is `<stage>[ n]: <unit>`; route-guard.py says the label
exists "so its time and cost join the change's record" and reserves `other: <name>` for "work with no change". This note is
work of a change. relay_metrics.py:203 groups unmatched agents as "other:"+unit, and :221-224 writes each such group to
.relay/changes/<name>/sweep-<stamp>.json. cycle.js:121 says the unit of a label is the full queue item id "so the metrics then
match it exactly"; the new label breaks that. The same choice also truncates (slice(0,70)) long labels so attempts 1 and 2 of a
long item get one identical label: for item relay-doctor-does-not-name-a-main-checkout-whose and "fix red gate 1" both become
"other: dead-fix-red-gate-1-relay-doctor-does-not-name-a-main-checkout-". Using the dead agent's own unit removes both.
evidence: truncation probe: both n=1 and n=2 print "other: dead-fix-red-gate-1-relay-doctor-does-not-name-a-main-checkout-"
git ls-files .relay/changes | grep -c sweep -> 177 (sweeps do store unmatched units as folders)
failing_case: The note agent is labelled "other: dead-gate-1-a-dead-workflow-agent-leaves-no-error-text-1". The ledger keeps unit
"dead-gate-1-a-dead-workflow-agent-leaves-no-error-text-1"; relay_metrics.match_unit returns None for it (no exact slug,
40-char prefix differs), so the sweep writes .relay/changes/dead-gate-1-a-dead-workflow-agent-leaves-no-error-text-1/sweep-<stamp>.json:
one new committed folder per dead attempt (21 deaths over 24-28 Oct would have made 21), and the note's time and cost are not
in the change's record. Expected: the note agent's unit is the dead agent's unit, so it joins the change's record.
fix_hint: In deadNote take the unit from the dead agent's label (the part after the first ": ") and label the note
`other: ${unit}`; keep the file name dead-<slug of the full label>-<n>.txt. Drop the slice. Update the test to assert the
note label and the file path separately.
pass_cases: 1. Unit item "the-item", "gate 1: the-item" throws once then is green: the note agent's label is "other: the-item" (or another
label whose unit part is exactly "the-item"); the result is ready; the note prompt still names
<scratch>/reports/dead-gate-1-the-item-1.txt, the error text and the label "gate 1: the-item".
2. relay_metrics.match_unit on that note agent (unit "the-item", stage "other") returns "the-item".
3. Every label the cycle starts still matches the ledger's grammar (tests/test_cycle_workflow.py:422).
4. No throw: no note agent starts (labels unchanged from today).
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py:255 asserts label "other: x" (unit of the dead agent).
findings.summary: the note runner's label names a unit of its own (dead-gate-1-<item>-1), so its cost misses the change and the sweep stores a new .relay/changes folder per death

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Labels repeat across runs of one unit: changeUnit and fixUnit both start "gate 1: <lab(it)>" (newState
resets gn), both use "fix: <lab(it)>" and "check: <lab(it)>". The file name is built from the label only, and the prompt says
"Write the file", which replaces it. cycle.js:123 records the rule this breaks: "File names carry the kind for a fix or
recheck run, so it never overwrites what the change run wrote" (tag()). The notes exist to measure deaths across many runs
(21 of 1,296 over five days), so a lost note is lost data. Size: 10 minutes.
evidence: cycle.js:109 const file = `${S}/reports/dead-${slug}-${n}.txt` (label only, no kind, no time)
cycle.js:123 comment on tag(): "so it never overwrites what the change run wrote"
failing_case: In one session (one scratch folder): a change run of item the-item has "gate 1: the-item" die once -> note
<scratch>/reports/dead-gate-1-the-item-1.txt written. A later kind=fix run of the same item (fixUnit, fresh counters) has
"gate 1: the-item" die once -> the runner is told to "Write the file" with the same path, replacing the first note.
Expected: both deaths are on disk (the first note kept).
fix_hint: Tell the runner to append the three lines (create the file if missing), so the brief's file name stays and a second run adds
a record instead of replacing one; or put tag(it) in the name by passing it from the callers. Add a test asserting the prompt
says append / does not say overwrite.
pass_cases: 1. Two runs in one scratch, each with "gate 1: the-item" throwing once: the note prompt of the second run tells the runner
to keep what the file already holds (append, or pick the next free name), so two records exist after both runs.
2. One throw in one run: one note with label, time, error (today's brief pass case) still holds.
reason: tests/test_cycle_workflow.py:260 asserts the prompt says append; note-prompt text keeps earlier content.
findings.summary: a later cycle run on the same unit in the same scratch overwrites the earlier dead note, losing the evidence the change exists to keep

details: CONFIRMED by reading the harness (plugins/delegate/tests/fake-workflow.js answers by label, $throw supported) and the test,
which never makes a note agent throw. The catch is the only thing that keeps a note failure from crashing the unit; it is the
case most likely in practice (a death from an outage tends to kill the next agent too). Size: 5 minutes.
evidence: grep of tests/test_cycle_workflow.py: no answer keyed "other: dead-..." ; only "stage:other": DONE in GREEN
failing_case: Answers: "gate 1: x" -> [$throw, green], "other: dead-gate-1-x-1" -> $throw. With the catch in deadNote the unit goes on
(gate 1 retried, ready). Delete the try/catch: the throw escapes ask(), the unit ends "crash", and no test fails today.
fix_hint: Add the two cases above to the new test (key the note's answer by its label).
pass_cases: 1. gate 1 throws once, the note agent throws: labels go gate 1, note, gate 1; the change is ready.
2. gate 1 throws every attempt and every note throws: the stop detail is gate 1's error text, not the note's.
3. gate 1 throws once, the note succeeds: unchanged from today's test.
findings.summary: no test covers a note agent that itself dies; removing the try/catch in deadNote passes every test
